hero.title: Welcome to your daily kitchen of learning
hero.welcome: Welcome back, chefs. In this kitchen we choose hard, we prepare our mise en place, and we get 1% better every day. Start with your bell ringer, then take on today's challenge. Standards are earned through purposeful practice and feedback.

today.title: Today's learning objective
today.objective: Name the five classical mother sauces and identify the thickening agent used in each.
today.skill: Making a blond roux: equal weights of fat and flour, cooked gently without color, then cooled or tempered before liquid is added.

bellRinger.title: Daily bell ringer
bellRinger.intro: Two minutes. No notes. Retrieval makes memory stronger.

questions.stem: Which mother sauce is thickened with a roux and made with milk?
questions.explanation: Béchamel is milk thickened with a white roux. Velouté uses white stock instead of milk.
Mise en place is French for 'everything in its place' – organizing and preparing before you cook.

questions.stem: Which type of cooking uses liquid or steam to transfer heat?
questions.explanation: Moist-heat methods such as braising, poaching and steaming transfer heat through liquid or steam.

challenge.title: Culinary challenge of the day
challenge.intro: Five questions. Two minutes. Answer as many as you can before the timer ends.
challenge.pointsNote: Practice points only – not a grade.

questions.stem: Which mother sauce is an emulsion of egg yolks and clarified butter?
questions.explanation: Hollandaise is a warm emulsion of egg yolks and clarified butter, seasoned with lemon.

questions.stem: What is the classic ratio of a roux by weight?
questions.explanation: A classic roux is equal parts fat and flour by weight, cooked to the color the sauce requires.

questions.stem: Which bones make a brown stock?
questions.explanation: Brown stock uses roasted bones (and usually roasted mirepoix and tomato product) for color and flavor.

questions.stem: Which cooking method is best for a tough, connective-tissue-rich cut like beef chuck?
questions.explanation: Long, slow, moist-heat cooking (braising) converts collagen to gelatin and tenderizes tough cuts.

professionalism.title: Professionalism reminder
items: Professionalism is practiced, not simply discussed.
Arrive with your uniform ready, hair restrained, and hands washed.
Mise en place applies to the kitchen, to learning, and to life.
Clean as you go. Taste, adjust, and own your work.
